name: Preventing Recurring Wall and Ceiling Cracks From Showing Through Paint

mainEntity.name: How do interior painters in Los Angeles County deal with hairline cracks and recurring ceiling or wall cracks so they don’t just reappear after painting?
mainEntity.text: How do interior painters in Los Angeles County deal with hairline cracks and recurring ceiling or wall cracks so they don’t just reappear after painting?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Los Angeles County, hairline and recurring cracks in walls and ceilings are common due to minor settling, temperature changes, and past repairs. If not handled correctly, they often reappear shortly after a repaint. Instead of simply smearing spackle over a closed crack, professional painters should first open it slightly with a utility knife or scraper to create a V-shaped channel, which allows filler to bond properly. For stable hairline cracks, a high-quality, flexible patching compound may suffice, followed by sanding and priming. For recurring cracks, especially at seams or corners, embedding joint tape or fiberglass mesh in joint compound is more durable. After sanding smooth and priming, topcoats can be applied. Painters should also look for underlying causes: ongoing structural movement, moisture, or loose drywall/plaster. Some cracks associated with building movement may still return over time, even after careful repair, so many contractors exclude them from standard warranties or treat them as a separate scope. Discuss your specific cracks during the estimate, ask what repair methods they propose, and whether they expect long-term success. For severe or widening cracks, you may be referred to a contractor or structural professional before cosmetic painting is attempted.
acceptedAnswer.description: Los Angeles painters should address recurring cracks by identifying movement causes, opening and stabilizing the crack, using flexible fillers or tape, and priming before painting. Simple spackle alone often fails. Ask what repair method they use for hairline vs. structural cracks and whether these areas are excluded from standard warranties.
